_meta.WRITTEN_BY_AI: This list was written by an AI (Claude, by Anthropic). It has not been read by a native speaker of Mandarin. Every name needs a native reader's check before release: the characters, the meaning given, how natural the name sounds, and anything it might call to mind that the writer could not hear.
_meta.language: enUS display text; pinyin without tone marks
_meta.status: staging input for the catalogue importer; not yet reviewed by the owner or by a native reader
_meta.what_the_game_shows: Only the 'display' string: the pinyin and the English gloss, as in 'Mo Mo (Ink)'. No Chinese characters appear in game text. The 'characters' column exists only so a native reader can check each name.

vanilla_loc_pattern.key: Beaver.NamePool in enUS_names.csv: one key whose text is every name, one per line.
vanilla_loc_pattern.note: The vanilla pool is global and shared by every faction (docs/tech/two-peoples.md: BeaverNameService). Writing these names into Beaver.NamePool would rename beavers in Folktails and Iron Teeth games too, so the faction needs its own namer and its own keys.

suggested_mod_key_pattern.form: As vanilla: one key, the 'display' strings joined with line breaks. The CSV validator rejects empty lines, so no blank line inside the text.

field_rules.pinyin: Hanyu pinyin, no tone marks, each syllable capitalized and separated by a space.
field_rules.characters: The intended characters, simplified. For checking only.
field_rules.pattern: 'doubled' = one syllable said twice, the way most zoo pandas are named. 'xiao' = 'Little' plus one syllable, the other everyday way of making a pet name. 'two-syllable' = an ordinary two-syllable word used as a name.
field_rules.sure: 'high' = a common name or pet name with this meaning. 'medium' = a real word with this meaning that the writer believes is natural as a name, or a name with a homophone or an English reading worth a second look. 'low' = the writer doubts it; expect to replace it.
field_rules.note: What the checker should look at.

rules_followed: Every name is meant to be a real name or a real word with the stated meaning. No syllable was invented.
No name is used in both pools. The check is on the pinyin as displayed, so two names written with different characters but the same toneless spelling count as one.

Left out on purpose: names of well-known living pandas that the writer knows of (among them Le Le, An An, Bei Bei, Bao Bao, Jia Jia, De De, Kai Kai, Ke Ke, Ying Ying, Tuan Tuan, Yuan Yuan, Hua Hua, Meng Meng, Xiang Xiang, Xiao Xiao, Lei Lei, Xin Xin, Xing Xing, Liang Liang, Nuan Nuan, Yang Yang, Tian Tian, Ya Ya, Huan Huan, Qi Zai, Fu Bao). Le Le and An An appear as examples in the design documents; they are left out here for this reason and can be added back by the owner.

Left out on purpose: syllables that sound like bodily functions, insults, death or animals used as insults when doubled (for example Pi Pi, Pu Pu, Shi Shi, Niao Niao, Si Si, Ben Ben, Dai Dai, Sha Sha, Zhu Zhu, Gou Gou, Gua Gua, Que Que), doubled forms that are family words (Ba Ba, Ma Ma, Ge Ge, Ye Ye, Nai Nai, Shu Shu), and names that read badly in English (for example Dong Dong, Bang Bang, Du Du, Mu Mu, Die Die, You You).
No religious names. No names tied to the zodiac.
_meta.why_the_inkpaw_pool_has_two_patterns: The task asked for at least 120 doubled names. Once well-known pandas and unfortunate syllables are removed, the writer could find only 99 doubled names in toneless pinyin that it was willing to stand behind, and 43 of those are marked 'medium' or 'low'. Rather than pad the list with doubtful names, the pool is completed with 29 'Xiao' names, which are the other common way real pandas and real pets are named. The owner can ship the doubled names alone (99) or both (128).
_meta.recurring_characters: Four names from these pools are reserved for the small cast that future flavor text may quote (see STYLE.md): Nuo Nuo, Song Song, Dou Dou (Inkpaws) and Hua Jiao (Ringtail). If the checker rejects any of them, change the cast as well.
